analysis:
On 15 June 2019 Modi told the NITI Aayog Governing Council that the goal of a US$5 trillion economy by 2024 was challenging but achievable; the Economic Survey (4 July 2019) and Budget (5 July) set it out as a 2024-25 target with a base of about US$2.7 trillion.

World Bank data (fiscal-year labelling inferred) put nominal GDP at US$3.76 trillion in 2024-25 and US$3.96 trillion in 2025-26; the government told Parliament that the IMF April 2026 WEO figure for FY2025-26 is US$3.92 trillion. The target was therefore not met by 2024-25.

Nominal dollar GDP depends on the exchange rate as well as growth; the rupee depreciated in the period, and the 2020 contraction also affected the path. The government has since cited 2027-28 as the new date. There is ambiguity whether '2024' meant FY2023-24 or FY2024-25; under either reading the target was missed.
